results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system, as recorded in VFB. VFB describes the mushroom body as divided into: the calyx, which is closest to the cortex and receives sensory interneuron afferents; the pedunculus, which is a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes; and the mushroom body lobe system, which consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch, which have different structures at different life stages. VFB holds various data related to the mushroom body, including images, neurons with some part in the mushroom body, and parts of the mushroom body, with counts of [2](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of mushroom body") images, [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") neurons with some part in the mushroom body, and [176](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of mushroom body") parts of the mushroom body. For further information, you can explore the available data in VFB, such as listing all available images of mushroom body or neurons with synaptic terminals in mushroom body.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: The types of Kenyon cells in the adult Drosophila brain include [[KCab-c](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110929 "Open KCab-c in Virtual Fly Brain")(i)](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049111 "Open KCab-c(i) in Virtual Fly Brain"), KCab-c, [KCg-m](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111061 "Open KCg-m in Virtual Fly Brain"), [[Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain") of main calyx](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047926 "Open Kenyon cell of main calyx in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100247 "Open gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), as well as alpha/beta Kenyon cell, alpha'/beta' Kenyon cell, and adult gamma Kenyon cell. VFB records show that there are several subclasses of Kenyon cell, with [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") listed. These can be further subdivided into subtypes such as core, surface, posterior, anterior-posterior, middle, and dorsal. VFB holds 37 records of subclasses of Kenyon cell, and also has annotated scRNAseq data for Kenyon cell, transgene expression in Kenyon cell, downstream connectivity classes for Kenyon cell, and upstream connectivity classes for Kenyon cell. To explore the specific characteristics of each type, you can query the available images of Kenyon cell, which VFB holds [32328](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of Kenyon cell") records of.

results.title: Basic connectivity
results.question: What are the main input neurons to the mushroom body?
results.response: The main input neurons to the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are sensory interneurons, according to the VFB database. VFB records show that the calyx, which is closest to the cortex, receives sensory interneuron afferents. Additionally, VFB data indicates that other main input neurons to the mushroom body include projection neurons from the antennal lobe, as well as sensory interneuron afferents to the calyx and neurons with presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body. This includes larval antennal lobe multiglomerular projection neurons and larval uniglomerular projection neurons. VFB holds [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") records of neurons with some part in the mushroom body, [601](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsSynaptic "Run in VFB: Neurons with synaptic terminals in mushroom body") records of neurons with synaptic terminals in the mushroom body, and [366](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body") records of neurons with presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body, which may provide further information on the connectivity of the mushroom body.

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response:
The [LPLC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrch0cuk "Open LPLC2 in Virtual Fly Brain") visual neuron type is characterized as a Lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron with specific characteristics and functions. According to VFB, its cell body is located in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind. The LPLC2 neuron has a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer, extending outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer, allowing it to detect looming stimuli. In the lobula, it has its main dendritic arbors in layers 4 and 5B, with minor processes in layer 5A, and presynaptic sites in layer 4. 

VFB records show that the LPLC2 neuron projects to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP, anterior to LPLC1 and dorsal to LC4. Its activity is associated with a jump escape response. The connectome data indicates that the arbors of LPLC2 neurons span approximately 25 lobula optic columns, overlapping with other LPLC2 cells. VFB holds data on approximately 80 of these cells per optic lobe, and they are predicted as cholinergic. 

VFB does not currently hold comprehensive data on all connections of the LPLC2 neuron type. However, the available data can be used to explore its connections and function further. Follow-up queries can be used to investigate the specific connections and relationships of the LPLC2 neuron type in more detail.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior, with a unique anatomy and connectivity profile. According to VFB, it has a large cell body located posterior to the lower protocerebrum, and its large descending axon is several times larger than any other axon in the cervical connective. The giant fiber neuron enters the cervical connective via the posterior cerebro-cervical fascicle and descends on the ipsilateral side, in the dorsal cervical fasciculus. In the brain, it has dendritic arborization in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center, where it receives substantial input from zone A and B Johnston organ neurons.

VFB records show that there are several driver lines available for the giant fiber neuron, including [P{R48A11-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R30C01-p65.AD} expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBtp0121835FBtp0118557 "Open P{R48A11-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R30C01-p65.AD} expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain"), [P{R68A06-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R25C08-p65.AD} expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBtp0116198FBtp0118471 "Open P{R68A06-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R25C08-p65.AD} expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [P{GMR91H05-GAL4} expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBtp0064022 "Open P{GMR91H05-GAL4} expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain"). 

The connectivity of the giant fiber neuron is characterized by downstream connectivity classes ([389](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records in VFB) and upstream connectivity classes ([472](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records in VFB). 

Relevant publications for the giant fiber neuron include Thomas and Wyman (1984), Koto et al. (1981), and Namiki et al. (2018), as well as other studies such as Power (1948), Ito et al. (2014), Kamikouchi et al. (2009), Matsuo et al. (2016), and Kim et al. (2020). 

VFB holds a range of data on the giant fiber neuron, including [23](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") images of DNp01, [5](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,SplitsTargeting "Run in VFB: Splits targeting DNp01") splits targeting DNp01, [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") records of transgene expression in DNp01, and connectivity data.
